 Oral Judgment
1.
This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement.

2. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 31.03.2017,
Muniyappa, a 55 year old died.
3. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month notionally since there was no evidence as to the actual income of the deceased.

In such circumstances, since the accident is of the year 2017, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which would be Rs.11,000/-.

Since the deceased was aged 55 years, future prospects of 10% requires to be added to the same,
which makes his income to be Rs.12,100/-.

Since the deceased has two dependants, 1/3rd requires to be NC: 2024:KHC:45989 deducted from the same, which makes his income to be Rs.8,066/-.
4.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.10,64,712/- (Rs.8,066/- X 12 X '11' ) towards 'loss of dependency'.
5.

The claimants would also be entitled to Rs.48,400/-
each towards 'loss of love and affection', which would be Rs.2,90,400/- (Rs.48,400/- X 6 members).

They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- towards 'miscellaneous expenses'.
6.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,91,412/- as against Rs.11,87,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization.
7. However, the claimant would not be entitled to interest for the delayed period in filing this appeal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
9. The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
10. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.

Sd/-
